name: The Pale Meridian Engines
description:
A Circuit institution since 2197, The Pale Meridian Engines have spent nearly three decades playing worker pubs, union halls, and the kind of mid-tier venues that smell like recycled coolant and fried protein. The founding trio — Solange Abara-Lindqvist on hammered dulcimer and vocals, Renzo Cho-Nkemdirim on upright bass and harmonica, and the late Pita Vasile-Osei on drums — built their sound from the sediment of everything their grandparents' generation had carried into the megacity: Hawaiian slack-key guitar traditions, Congolese likembe patterns, Scandinavian drone harmonics, and the particular exhausted poetry of people who work shifts that don't end when they're supposed to.

After Vasile-Osei's death from industrial lung disease in 2214, the band nearly dissolved. They returned a year later with new drummer Kezia Mwangi-Hartmann and a rawer, more mournful sound that somehow made them more beloved than before. Their album 'The Second Shift' — released on physical vinyl and distributed through Circuit record shops — is one of the best-selling physical media releases in GLMZ history, a fact Vantablack Media finds deeply inconvenient since they don't own the masters.
creator: Solange Abara-Lindqvist
genre: circuit folk, working blues, acoustic drone
audience: Tier 2 working class, shift workers, union members, Tier 3 nostalgia listeners, older Tier 1 residents
cultural_impact: The Pale Meridian Engines are the Circuit's shared memory made audible. Their songs document the lived texture of working-class life in GLMZ — the broken transit lines, the debt cycles, the love affairs conducted in twenty-minute lunch breaks — with a specificity that no corporate-produced music has ever managed. They have turned down Vantablack Media contracts three times, a fact recounted in Circuit culture with something approaching reverence. When Pita Vasile-Osei died, the outpouring of grief across Tier 2 was described by commentators as the largest spontaneous public mourning since the Blackout Riots.
story_hooks: Vantablack Media is making a fourth attempt to acquire the band's back catalog through a shell company, and Solange Abara-Lindqvist needs someone to trace the ownership chain before she signs anything.
A rare original pressing of 'The Second Shift' has surfaced in a Tier 1 pawn shop — its provenance suggests it belonged to someone who died in an event the official record says never happened.

Kezia Mwangi-Hartmann has been approached by a Spire talent agency and is secretly considering leaving the band — if word gets out before she decides, the fallout could fracture Circuit solidarity networks that use the band as a unifying symbol.
